title: When the Tide Turns
premise: Bram Voss, a jaded wedding planner recovering from a betrayal that ended his own engagement, is hired to orchestrate the season's final wedding on Saltglass Island — only to discover the venue, Marrow Orchard, is co-owned by Wren Halloway, the woman who walked out on him seven years ago. Neither can sell their half without the other's signature, and neither will budge: Bram needs the fee to save his failing business, while Wren is fighting to keep the orchard her late grandmother left them both. Forced into uneasy collaboration as the wedding deadline and the last ferry of the season close in, they unearth the truth of why Wren left — a letter Bram's mother intercepted to protect him from leaving with her. At the climax, Bram chooses truth over loyalty to his family, publicly reading the letter at the wedding he almost sabotaged; in the end, Wren signs the deed not to sell but to make the orchard theirs together, and they board the last ferry not to leave the island but to bring the first guests of a new life back across.
about_author: Casper Whitlock spent a decade planning weddings on coastal islands before trading clipboards for manuscripts, and it shows in every tide-timed kiss. They write romances about people who mistake stubbornness for self-protection, from a drafty house overlooking a ferry terminal.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry Season
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram loses a client mid-ceremony when the groom bolts, cementing his belief that weddings are beautiful lies. His business teeters on bankruptcy until an offer arrives: plan a high-profile wedding at Marrow Orchard on Saltglass Island. The beat: weary cynicism masking desperation.

chapters.title: A Deed With Two Names
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Arriving on the island, Bram reviews the venue contract and discovers the orchard has two owners — one signature already given, one withheld. The second name makes his stomach drop: Wren Halloway. The beat: dread dressed up as professional composure.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Kept the Orchard
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren tends her grandmother's apple trees, refusing calls from lawyers and developers. When she learns the co-owner coming to town is Bram Voss, she resolves to stall him until after harvest. The beat: grief hardened into defiance.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Bad Timing
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram and Wren collide at the dock over a crate of cider apples, all sharp words and old muscle memory. She refuses to sign; he reveals he'll lose everything without this wedding. The beat: anger that keeps slipping into intimacy.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Cornered by debt on the orchard herself, Wren proposes a truce: Bram plans the wedding, she gets through harvest, and neither mentions the past. Both sign an absurdly formal agreement. The beat: wary alliance, hands careful not to touch.

chapters.title: The Guest List Problem
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The bride, socialite Delphine Marsh, demands impossible changes; worse, her guest list includes Bram's mother, Odile, who hasn't set foot on the island since Bram was a boy. Bram realizes Odile grew up here. The beat: unease he can't file under logistics.

chapters.title: Cider and Confessions
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Late-night pressing apples, Wren finds Bram asleep in the barn and wakes him with cider. He offers a sanitized version of his engagement's collapse; she gives nothing back. The beat: warmth arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Letters
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Sorting her grandmother Maren's things, Wren finds letters hinting Maren deliberately left the orchard to both of them — a matchmaker's last trick. Wren burns the most revealing one. The beat: guilt over a truth half-destroyed.

chapters.title: Storm Damage
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A gale tears the ceremony tent and floods the tasting room. Working through the night to salvage the orchard, Bram and Wren fall into easy rhythm — then catch themselves laughing and go cold. The beat: the past asserting itself through shared competence.

chapters.title: Odile Arrives
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram's mother lands on the island unannounced, charming everyone, and goes strangely pale at the sight of the orchard's east gate. She urges Bram to buy Wren out fast. The beat: filial loyalty beginning to chafe.

chapters.title: The Wedding That Isn't Yours
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren watches Bram coax Delphine's wedding into something genuinely lovely and hates how well she remembers this version of him. Delphine, perceptive, asks Wren if she's the reason the planner looks haunted. The beat: jealousy of a life unlived.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Short-staffed, Bram picks apples beside Wren's ragtag crew of islanders who adopt him as one of their own. Found family forms around bonfires and bad singing. The beat: belonging sneaking past his defenses.

chapters.title: An Intercepted Past
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confronts Odile at the inn, revealing she once wrote Bram asking him to come away with her — and never got an answer. Odile's face says everything before her mouth denies it. The beat: the shape of the betrayal becoming visible.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Odile tells Bram Wren abandoned him for a sailing life, doubling down on the old story. Bram wants to believe her, because the alternative means his whole childhood was curated. The beat: the comfort of a lie meeting its cost.

chapters.title: Delphine's Doubts
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Bride Delphine gets cold feet and, unexpectedly, confides in Wren — she saw how Bram looked at Wren during the storm cleanup. Wren insists it's ancient history. The beat: a mirror held up, unwelcome.

chapters.title: The East Gate Key
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram finds an old key in Maren's effects labeled with his childhood nickname and the east gate. Odile snatches it away, too fast. The beat: suspicion taking root where trust used to be.

chapters.title: First Frost
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. An early frost threatens the crop; the whole island turns out to harvest through the night. Bram works beside Wren until dawn, and afterward, half-frozen, they almost kiss in the barn doorway. The beat: desire outrunning caution.

chapters.title: The Almost
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The near-kiss hangs between them for days. Bram finally asks why she left; Wren says she asked him a question once and silence was his answer. Bram has no memory of any letter. The beat: two truths that can't both be true.

chapters.title: What Odile Kept
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren pressures Odile privately; Odile admits she 'protected' Bram from a girl who'd have taken him to sea, but claims Wren never truly waited. A partial confession, weaponized. The beat: sympathy for the villain, briefly.

chapters.title: Sabotage Season
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Delphine's fiancé's family pushes to move the wedding off-island, threatening Bram's fee. Wren offers the orchard free if he stays. Pride flares; he accepts anyway. The beat: dependence turning tender.

chapters.title: Maren's Matchmaking
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds Maren's diary: entries about a boy named Bram, the east gate left unlocked on purpose, and a line — 'some fences are meant to be climbed, not kept.' Wren weeps among the trees. The beat: inheritance redefined.

chapters.title: The Letter Hunt
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Armed with fragments, Bram searches Odile's rented cottage and finds a locked tin. Inside: Wren's seven-year-old letter, unopened, plus train tickets Odile bought to keep him home. The beat: the floor dropping out of his history.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Inn
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram faces Odile; she breaks down, confessing she chose his stability over his happiness after his father left. He walks out without forgiving her. The beat: love and fury occupying the same breath.

chapters.title: Telling Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Bram brings Wren the letter, still sealed, and lets her open it. Her own young voice, full of hope, undoes them both. But Wren can't forgive instantly — seven years don't fold flat. The beat: vindication without resolution.

chapters.title: Too Little, Too Late?
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram asks for a real chance; Wren refuses, saying she won't be someone's second choice after a revelation. She throws the truce agreement back at him. The beat: pride as armor, again, but thinner.

chapters.title: Delphine Decides
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Delphine, transformed by island life, tells her fiancé she wants a small wedding or none — and tells Wren that watching her and Bram waste time is the saddest thing she's seen. The beat: the bride becomes the catalyst.

chapters.title: The Deed Deadline
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The developer's offer expires in ten days; signing means the orchard survives only as a resort backdrop. Wren digs in. Bram, caught between his fee and her trees, chooses to walk away from his payment. The beat: sacrifice offered quietly.

chapters.title: Why Bram Doesn't Believe
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren learns the full story of Bram's ruined engagement — his partner left him at the altar and took the business's seed money. She sees his cynicism as scar tissue, not character. The beat: compassion replacing resentment.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner Ruin
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Odile attends the rehearsal dinner uninvited; Wren defends Bram against his own mother's smoothing-over. Publicly humiliated, Odile threatens to contest the deed. The beat: family loyalty inverted — found family standing firmer than blood.

chapters.title: The Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A historic storm is forecast for the wedding date; evacuation ferries may run early, meaning the last ferry of the season could leave without anyone aboard by choice. Stakes compress: weather, deadline, heart. The beat: the clock audibly ticking.

chapters.title: Boarding Up Together
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Preparing the orchard for the storm, Bram and Wren nail boards over the east gate — and Wren finally tells him she stayed all these years partly hoping he'd come find her. The beat: honesty as the truest shelter.

chapters.title: Odile's Choice
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Odile, chastened by the islanders' quiet kindness during storm prep, delivers the missing piece: Maren wrote to her too, begging her to let Bram choose. Odile gives Bram Maren's final letter. The beat: the antagonist choosing grace.

chapters.title: Maren's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Maren's letter, read aloud in the barn, names both grandchildren and asks them to be brave enough to lose each other once more before keeping each other forever. Wren takes Bram's hand. The beat: permission granted by the dead.

chapters.title: The Wedding Day Storm
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The storm hits hours before the ceremony; the tent fails, the power dies, and Delphine's guests panic. Bram, who planned perfection for a living, improvises a candlelit wedding inside the cider barn. The beat: chaos transfigured into beauty.

chapters.title: Vows Overheard
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Watching Bram officiate improvised vows, Wren hears him say marriage is 'the bravest lie two people agree to tell' — then watch him correct himself: 'the bravest truth.' Their eyes meet across the barn. The beat: belief returning like blood to a numb limb.

chapters.title: The Developer's Last Offer
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The developer appears mid-reception with a final contract. In front of the whole island, Bram tears it up — forfeiting his fee, his rescue, his old life. Wren witnesses it. The beat: public choice, private consequence.

chapters.title: Climax: The Letter Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the reception's peak, Bram stands and reads Wren's seven-year-old letter aloud, then Odile's confession, owning his mother's lie and his own blindness. He asks Wren not for forgiveness but for a first chance, properly dated. The beat: truth chosen over loyalty, at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Two Signatures
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren answers by fetching the deed and signing it — not to sell, but naming the orchard jointly held, forever. The islanders cheer; Delphine catches the bouquet straight into Wren's arms. The beat: the grand gesture answered with a legal, binding tenderness.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry Departs
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Morning after the storm, the season's final ferry loads up. Odile boards it, heading home to make amends elsewhere; Delphine and her new husband wave from the rail. Bram and Wren stand on the dock, letting it go without them. The beat: release, and staying as an act of love.

chapters.title: When the Tide Turns
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Weeks later, the orchard hosts its first small wedding — planned by Bram, catered by the island, witnessed by found family. Under the east gate, now permanently unlocked, Bram asks Wren to stay not for a season but always. She says yes before he finishes. The beat: second chances, perfectly timed at last.
